name: Andrew Cuomo
role: Governor of New York (2011-2021); state attorney general (2007-2010); US HUD secretary (1997-2001); 2025 New York City mayoral candidate
summary: Andrew Cuomo is a Democrat whose record combines progressive social and labor measures with fiscal restraint and a tough-on-crime posture. As governor he signed marriage equality, the SAFE Act gun law, a $15 minimum wage, paid family leave and climate legislation, while capping property taxes and restraining spending. In his 2025 mayoral run he stressed policing, housing supply and opposition to higher taxes on the wealthy.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Said that cutting police leads to more crime and pledged 5,000 more officers.

abortion-legal.rationale: Said it is her body, her choice, signed the 2019 Reproductive Health Act and proposed writing Roe v. Wade rights into the state constitution.

central-planning.rationale: Says socialism has not succeeded anywhere and that Americans do not want to dismantle the economic system; calls for 'responsible capitalism'.

corporate-influence.rationale: Described Citizens United as unleashing a flood of dark money that drowns out ordinary voices and pushed to close the LLC loophole in campaign finance.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Raised the state's minority- and women-owned business contracting goal from 20 to 30 percent in 2014 and proposed extending it to state-funded contracts (2016 policy book); framed cannabis legalization as reducing 'impacts of criminalization affecting communities of color' (2019 policy book).

death-penalty.rationale: Proposed formally abolishing the death penalty in 2019, calling it archaic and discriminatory, and said his father believed state-sanctioned killing appealed to our worst impulses.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Described the social safety net as a moral imperative and expanded SNAP outreach, though his book also urged earlier welfare reform; evidence leans against cutting welfare.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Signed New York into the National Popular Vote compact in 2014 (and made membership permanent in 2016), saying that 'by aligning the Electoral College with the voice of the nation's voters' it ensures 'the equality of votes'. He backs the national popular vote deciding the presidency through the compact rather than abolishing the Electoral College outright.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Championed the Women's Equality Act, pay equity law and equal treatment for women.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Launched a Green New Deal, set a goal of 100 percent clean power by 2040 and signed the 2019 climate law.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said Marriage Equality's passage affirmed that all New Yorkers are equal under the law and pushed antidiscrimination laws.

ethnic-nation.rationale: His HUD speech says America was founded on nationhood without common ancestry or color, welcoming people of every race.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Banned high-volume fracking, pledged to end coal use and set a goal of 100 percent clean power.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Mixed: he secured the closure of Indian Point as unsafe but said the state must support upstate nuclear plants.

flat-income-tax.rationale: In his 2012 State of the State address he said 'a flat tax is not a fair tax', and in a December 2011 op-ed called it unfair that $20,000 and $20 million of taxable income faced the same marginal rate; the 2011 tax law he pushed added brackets.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Signed marriage equality and pushed the Gender Expression Non-Discrimination Act, writing that discrimination against transgender New Yorkers 'in housing, employment and public accommodations' is 'unacceptable' (2019 policy book); his 2015 regulations barred discrimination on gender identity.

future-generations.rationale: Said it is vital to commit to a greener future to preserve natural beauty for children and grandchildren.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Created the NY Council on Women and Girls in 2017 and used it for initiatives on pay equity and student debt.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Proposed passing the Gender Identity and Expression Non-Discrimination Act, regulations protecting transgender people and easier ID changes, and support for transgender troops.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Proposed a Middle Class Child Care Tax Credit and made the non-custodial earned income tax credit permanent.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 2024 and 2025 said true friends fight for the state of Israel and rejected 'occupation' language as meaning Israel has no right to exist as a Jewish state.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Mixed record: he signed recreational cannabis legalization for adults in 2021, but his September 2025 speech opposes legalizing the drug trade more broadly. His September 2025 speech opposes legalizing the drug trade; this is broader than his enacted cannabis exception.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: In a 2025 debate he attacked an opponent's stance on prostitution as making it legal for prostitutes.

limit-guns.rationale: Signed the NY SAFE Act in 2013 with an assault weapons ban, magazine limits and expanded background checks, and later backed red flag laws.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: His September 2025 op-ed endorses responsible capitalism, with safeguards, rather than abandoning private enterprise for socialism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His record is of an activist state: paid family leave, minimum wage, rent law, free tuition and public investment, and he describes government as the collective.

open-borders.rationale: Criticized opening the borders with no plan, while also supporting lawful immigration and the state DREAM Act.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Criticized Don't Ask, Don't Tell for discrimination against LGBTQ veterans and proposed supporting transgender troops.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Mixed: of the 2021 carbon-fee bill (Climate and Community Investment Act) he said 'I understand the concept, and the concept, it makes sense' but 'you can't do it that way', questioning its economic impact; as governor he relied mainly on mandates and subsidies for clean power.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Held off fracking pending a Health Department study and then prohibited it citing health risks.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: He defended the Columbus statue as Italian-American heritage while signing restrictions on Confederate symbols in state settings.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Proposed comprehensive reform of the Freedom of Information Law to improve transparency, including extending it to the Legislature.

public-ownership.rationale: Rejects the socialist platform (free buses, rent freeze) as failing when tried; favors 'private enterprise with guardrails'.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Proposed and secured a statewide minimum wage rising to $15 and called the current wage unlivable; 2025 platform proposed $20.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Said New York should stand up for immigrants and in 2025 backed lawful immigration as a city of immigrants, while saying criminals should not be harbored.

rehabilitation.rationale: Funded college courses in prisons, proposed sentence reductions for rehabilitative programming and raised the age of juvenile jurisdiction.

religious-nation.rationale: In the same speech he says shared religion is unnecessary for belonging to the American nation.

rent-control.rationale: Signed 2019 law that strengthened rent regulation and called it the greatest expansion in four decades; in 2025 he opposed a rent freeze but promised stricter enforcement of rent stabilization.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: His April 2025 speech urges stopping foreign funding that dictates biased university curricula.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wrote that the best teacher is practice rather than theory.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Led the push for and signed the 2011 Marriage Equality Act; said the state finally tore down the barrier.

separated-powers.rationale: In August 2026 he welcomes congressional opposition as a check on an overly dominant president.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Proposed requiring comprehensive, medically accurate sex education including consent in grades 6 through 12.

social-market-economy.rationale: He advocates private enterprise with labor and consumer protections and social safety nets.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directed state funds toward chosen sectors through Regional Economic Development Councils, the NY Green Bank, Buffalo investment and tax-free innovation zones.

state-harmful.rationale: Said government is not an alien being, it is us, and that he believes in the collective model.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The 2018 book defends state payment of eligible graduates’ first two years of student-loan bills.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His 2019 State of the State book (p. 134 of the PDF) faults 'a federal government determined to cut us off from the rest of the world' for imposing 'damaging tariffs' that restrict markets and raise costs for New York farms.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Mixed: he signed a 2011 tax increase on high earners (extended to 2027) and in 2021 said the wealthy should pay more, but in 2025 warned that doubling taxes on the wealthy would drive them away.

term-limits.rationale: His 2018 book proposes eight-year legislative limits and statewide limits; he subsequently sought further gubernatorial terms himself.

unions-good.rationale: Wrote that labor unions protect fairness at the bargaining table and signed a 2018 law protecting public-sector union membership after Janus, which he called devastating to unions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mixed: in 2017 he called the federal Medicare for All plan a good idea and a state single-payer system an exciting possibility, but later voiced cost concerns; he also codified ACA protections and expanded Medicaid.

notes:
Positions rest mainly on his State of the State books (2016, 2017, 2019, 2020), compiled quotes from his books and speeches, and 2025 campaign coverage. Earlier State of the State addresses (2011-2015, 2018, 2021) and his books were not available as full text. Positions on taxes on the wealthy and on cannabis changed or were mixed over time.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: His father Mario Cuomo's positions are not used. Most recent position wins on taxes (he signed higher rates on top earners in 2011 and 2021 but opposes 'tax the rich' in 2026). The campaign-site op-ed text was read through a summarizing fetch tool. NYT and governor.ny.gov pages were not reachable, so governor-era laws rest on his own record page, the state program page and Wikipedia.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 12 answers taken from it, 21 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent third pass, no existing answers copied. Reviewed all 490 statements and the ranked table. Core new sources are HUD’s full address, the 2018 and 2021 policy books, and speaker-labelled 2025 debate material. Ethnic-nation is answered from an explicit statement that common ancestry and color are unnecessary for nationhood. The 2025 responsible-capitalism op-ed answers neither-capitalism-nor-communism negatively; centrist opposition to extremists alone does not establish left-right-obsolete. His appeal to Jewish voters to mobilize against antisemitism is not generalized into a doctrine that all racial groups should organize separate political interests. No evidence established ancestry-based transnational union, a linguistic definition of nationhood, kin-territorial claims, revolutionary strategy, class determinism or ethnic economic ownership. Progressive rebirth rhetoric concerns political reform, not radical national regeneration from decadence. The 2018 term-limit proposal is weighed against later reelection bids. Nursing-home-data concealment is weighed against transparency pledges. Tax policy changed: the August 2026 explicit opposition is the most recent position, superseding his governor-era tax increases. Cannabis legalization is not a position on every recreational drug: the broader drug answer uses the explicit 2025 opposition to legalizing the drug trade. Boycott evidence concerns Israel specifically; no opinion on excluding every religious minority is assumed. His sexual-harassment findings and resignation were reviewed as well as his legal reforms; no unrelated position was inferred from misconduct. Speech claims about legislation were cross-checked with the governing record; primary rhetorical positions are medium, enacted signature measures high. Failed direct campaign downloads are retained, and the usable browser-extracted text is saved separately. No living-person inferred answers.

claude-opus-5-5 deepening pass (2026-10-31) on line 14: added direct election of the head of state +1 medium (2014 National Popular Vote compact signing statement), tariffs -1 medium (2019 State of the State book on 'damaging tariffs'), pollution taxes 0 low (2021 carbon-fee bill: concept 'makes sense' but 'you can't do it that way'). Searched without a usable answer: ICC (only his defence of Netanyahu against one warrant, a nearby case, left null), binding fiscal rules (his 2 percent spending cap was a self-imposed budget practice, not a legal borrowing limit; no debt-cap proposal of his found), deficit stimulus, Amazon HQ2 incentives (not a position on business privileges as such), elites and the educated (his 2024 op-ed calls the Democratic Party elitist and disconnected, not political elites in general), strikes, gradual change. MediaSum CNN/NPR transcripts searched for Electoral College, term limits, deficits, tariffs, carbon tax, Amazon and stimulus. Three older answers that cited only OnTheIssues or Wikipedia were re-sourced to his own texts, values unchanged: flat income tax (2012 State of the State transcript, Dec 2011 op-ed), correcting racial injustice (2016 and 2019 policy books), freedom to discriminate (2019 policy book, campaign record page).
